correctness.rationale: At \(J=J_p=h=0\) the Hamiltonian is identically zero, so a fixed-root binary Ising system on \(|V_n|\) vertices has exactly \(2^{|V_n|-1}\) unit-weight configurations. The source uses \(|V_n|=2^{n+1}-1\). Direct substitution \(\theta=\phi=u=1\) into Theorem 1 gives \(128^{2^{n-1}-1}\), which differs already at \(n=2\). The corresponding free-energy coefficients are exactly \(1\) and \(7/4\) times \(\log2/\beta\).

value.rationale: Theorems 1 and 2 are central exact thermodynamic claims. The discrepancy is substantive: the finite-volume count is already wrong at \(n=2\), becomes exponentially wrong, and the limiting free-energy density is too large by a factor \(7/4\). The paper explicitly proposes this self-similarity construction for thermodynamic calculations and extension to other lattice models, so the state-count obstruction has direct methodological value.
